comparisons.basis: The complete Memento for the living in Wilson's 1915 Gregorian main text, printed page 2, is aligned with the ordered Memento and Et omnium blocks of Cummiskey's 1861 Canon. Wilson follows R (Reginae 337), with other manuscript readings in the apparatus; this is comparison through a critical edition, not direct manuscript collation or asserted descent.

comparisons.apparatus_caveat: Only these complete bounded prayer selections have been collated; this is not a full Ordinary or full missal diff. Printed 1606 and 1657 dates are witness dates, not proof of each variant’s introduction. The 1655 mandate and cited general chapters are separate contextual evidence. Long s, display initials, nasal abbreviations and line wraps are normalized as declared in the owning artifacts; source accents, u/v, ligatures, abbreviations and short endings otherwise remain. Spoken blocks and rubric positions remain recoverable; the 1657 (vel meis) is a printed alternative, not simultaneous speech. No immediate predecessor relationship, complete Romanization, or modern liturgical authorization is inferred.

comparisons.basis: The complete Orate invitation and response dialogue in each identified edition share the invitation to pray for acceptance of the sacrifice. The 1606 Dominus sit in corde tuo response differs from the 1657 Suscipiat Dominus; the later printed alternative and final priestly Amen remain explicit. This is alignment of the same liturgical function, not a claim that the two response compositions are identical.

comparisons.apparatus_caveat: Only the selected collect entries have been transcribed and independently checked, not the entire formularies or books. Each is one continuous priestly block. Printed shortened conclusions Per. and Per Dominum nostrum. are retained without supplying a doxology. Abbreviations, long s, u/v, ae ligatures and line layout are normalized as declared in the artifacts. The separate retained pages establish the changed Gospel and Sunday heading; those observations are not represented as full Gospel transcriptions. Printing dates do not date the introduction of the changes; intervening editions and immediate ancestry remain unestablished.
comparisons.basis: The complete printed collect entries in two Suscepimus Deus formularies perform the same liturgical function but are different compositions: Deus cuius providentia in 1550 and Largire nobis in 1604. The named formulary supplies the pairing anchor. The earlier heading is Dominica octava after Trinity; the later heading is Dominica sexta after the octave of Trinity. No identical numbered Sunday is assumed.

comparisons.apparatus_caveat: This is one dated calendar cell, not a claim that Teresa is absent from every part of the 1574 missal or that the whole calendar has been collated. Other computistical columns are omitted. The 1621 printed date remains October 5 and is not modernized to October 15. Abbreviations, ampersands and the cōm. macron are preserved; e-caudata/ligature and long s are normalized as declared. The printed common-Mass reference at p.409 is separately retained, with manuscript alterations excluded. Exact introduction date, chapter intervention and immediate textual ancestry remain unestablished.
comparisons.basis: The same bounded printed October 5 calendar row is compared in two Carmelite missals. In 1574 the date numeral is present and its feast cell is empty; the normalized body is therefore only 5. In 1621 the cell names Teresa, duplex minus, with Placidus and companions commemorated and page reference 409. Calendar entries are explicitly typed as calendar rows, not spoken prayers.

source_record.authority: The General Chapter of 1677, under Innocent Le Masson, Prior of the Grande Chartreuse and General of the Order
source_record.citation:
Printed on the engraved title page of the 1679 edition, READ HERE IN THE PAGE
IMAGE on 2026-08-02 and no longer taken from the catalogue: `MISSALE CARTVSIANI
/ Ordinis ex ordinatione Capituli Generalis. / Anno Domini M.D.C.LXXVII. /
Celebrati Sub R.P.D. Innocentio le Masson Priore / Cartusiæ ac totius eiusdem
ordinis Generali` [verified, canvas f5 of ark:/12148/bpt6k9127828m].

THE CATALOGUE'S TYPO IS THE CATALOGUE'S. Gallica's record transcribes the last
words as `totius eiusdem odinis generali`; the engraved plate reads `ordinis`
plainly. The earlier state of this row reproduced `odinis` and flagged it as the
catalogue's own -- that flag was right, and it is now settled at the plate
instead of being a guess about a transcription.

THE ORDINANCE ITSELF IS PRINTED IN THE BOOK, which is better evidence than the
title page and was not previously known to this file. Innocent Le Masson's
prefatory letter at canvas f7, headed `FRATER INNOCENTIVS, Humilis Prior Majoris
Cartusiæ, ac totius Ordinis Cartusiensis Minister Generalis`, recites it and
then quotes its tenor [verified in the page image]: `... ordinationem in Capitulo
Generali anni 1677. edidimus, cujus tenorem hic referre placet. [Quia Missalium
penuria laboramus, ordinamus Missalia ad vsum Ordinis de novo imprimi, ac
propterea monemus Visitatores Provinciarum & Priores Domorum, vt si quid in
ipsis ... addendum` -- the sentence runs onto the following leaf, which was not
fetched, and is therefore cut here at the catchword rather than completed from
guesswork.
source_record.date_note:
TWO YEARS ARE IN PLAY AND THEY ARE NOT COLLAPSED. The chapter met in 1677; the
book was printed in 1679. The station is dated by the PRINTING, 1679, because
that is the state the line reached, and the chapter's year is in `authority` and
in the citation rather than being averaged into the date.

BOTH YEARS ARE NOW VERIFIED ON ONE LEAF, which is the cleanest possible warrant
for keeping them apart: the engraved title plate at canvas f5 carries `Anno
Domini M.D.C.LXXVII.` in its title and `1679` in its imprint at the foot of the
same plate [verified 2026-08-02]. Le Masson's letter at f7 names the chapter
year a third time, as `Capitulo Generali anni 1677`.
source_record.effect: No departure. No unit of this use has been read.

TWO FACTS ABOUT THE COPY, recorded because neither was in this file. The
digitised exemplar is NOT a BnF copy: the manifest labels it `Bibliothèque
municipale de Grenoble, Vh.258 Rés.`, Gallica hosts it as part of the Grenoble
documentary set `BnGren00`, and a `BIBLIOTHEQUE DE GRENOBLE` stamp is visible on
the title plate itself [verified]. And the imprint, which the catalogue title
does not carry, is engraved at the foot of that plate: `FAVRATII IN SABAVDIA /
Typis Ludouici du Four Sereniss. Ducis Tipographi ordinary Sumptibus maioris
Cartusiæ / 1679`, signed `L. Cossin Sculpsit` -- printed at Fourvoirie in Savoy
at the charge of the Grande Chartreuse.

TWO WITNESSES OF ONE DECREE WERE COMPARED HERE, and the comparison is the
opposite of the one the base slice made. Both the 1970 typical edition's text
layer and the 2002 typical edition's print this decree, and both were read here:
the 1970 scan renders `eucharistice`, `Pontice`, `Pontihicis`, `adibus` and

source_record.citation: Sacred Congregation for Divine Worship, De editione typica altera, Prot. N. 1970/74, 27 March 1975, printed in the front matter of the 2002 typical edition; registered as work.holy-see.de-editione-typica-altera-missalis-romani-1975.
source_record.dateline: Ex aedibus Sacrae Congregationis pro Cultu Divino, die 27 martii Anni Sancti 1975, feria V in Cena Domini.
source_record.effect: No departure in this slice, and the act itself says why not.
source_record.effect_note:
THE ACT LISTS ITS OWN CHANGES AND NONE OF THEM IS IN THIS SLICE, which is a
better reason for an empty station than any this history has had before. Read
here: the description of the offices of acolyte and lector replaces those
treating of the subdeacon at nn. 142-152 of the Institutio generalis; certain
formularies of the ritual and votive Masses are completed with entrance and
communion antiphons; the Masses of the dedication of a church and altar, for
reconciliation, of the Blessed Virgin Mary Mother of the Church and of the Most
Holy Name of Mary are added; and further minor variations are made in titles and
rubrics. This slice carries the Ordinary and Holy Week, and the act touches
neither.

The acquisition audit calls this edition the postconciliar row with no whole
witness located anywhere -- what exists is the Ordo Missae alone, three orders of
magnitude too small. So the emptiness here is partly a real reading of the
decree and partly a bound on the corpus, and both are stated rather than one
being allowed to stand for the other.
source_record.instrument: De editione typica altera, Prot. N. 1970/74
source_record.parent_basis:
The act names what it follows: variations and additions have been introduced so
that this new edition may answer to the documents published since ITS FIRST
EDITION OF 1970. It names the 1970 edition rather than the 1971 reprint, and the
edge is drawn to the reprint because that is the state the line had reached; the
act reaches past it to the edition, and that is recorded here rather than
smoothed away.
source_record.parent_quotation:
Cum Missale Romanum denuo imprimendum sit, variationes et
additamenta inducta sunt, ut hæc nova editio respondeat documentis
post eiusdem primam editionem anno 1970 publici iuris factis.

source_record.authority: Sacred Congregation of Rites
source_record.citation:
Sacred Congregation of Rites, 9 December 1924, operative clause `Vaticana hujus
Missalis editio pro typica habenda est`, with later printings `omnino
conformandae erunt, ita ut in iis nihil immutare fas sit`; dateline `Die 9
Decembris 1924`, subscribed `A. Card. VICO, Ep. Portuen. et S. Rufinae, S. R. C.
Praefectus` and `Alexander Verde, S. R. C. Secretarius` [recorded, as above].
source_record.effect: No departure. No unit of this use has been read.
source_record.effect_note:
THIS STATION IS THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE THAT KEEPS A GENERALISATION HONEST, and it
is why the exempt-uses line is drawn the way it is. The two signatories here --
Cardinal Vico as Prefect and Alexander Verde as Secretary -- are THE SAME TWO MEN
who signed the Roman typical edition's decree of 25 July 1920, in the same
offices, four years apart. So the diocesan uses do not legislate their own
typical editions: Rome does, through the same congregation.

And yet no edge is drawn from the Roman line into this one. One congregation
acting for two rites is a fact about who signs, not a descent of one rite from
the other, and drawing it would make the Braga use look like a branch of the
Roman typical editions. The distinction between an authority and a lineage is
exactly what this file's edges exist to keep.

source_record.via_unrepresented_basis:
The same decree says the text was drawn from the other typical edition, that of
1900: `In qua editione, ex altera typica anni 1900 deprompta, illud tantum
innovatum est, quod ex recentibus praescriptionibus liturgicis et ex additionibus
et variationibus, in Breviario typico inductis, consequeretur.` That edition is
not in this corpus and no act promulgating it is cited here, so the edge from the
1634 revision down to 1920 crosses at least one station this record does not
hold. It is drawn as descent, not as succession.

The quotation also bounds the 1920 edition's own reach, and is why this act
carries so few departures: it says that the only thing made new was what followed
from the recent liturgical prescriptions and from the additions and variations
introduced in the typical Breviary.

source_record.act_citation_note:
CORRECTED 2026-08-01. This station carried `act_citation = "not-found"` from the
day it was drawn until the missal acquisition audit read the decree. The
correction, and why the error was made, are both worth keeping.

THE DECREE EXISTS AND HAS NOW BEEN READ, at page 2 of the Vatican typical
edition, in the exact facsimile this repository already had registered. Opening,
with the OCR damage of that text layer reproduced (`rubricanim`, `i960`):

  DECRETUM
  Novo rubricanim corpore, a Summo Pontifice Ioanne XXIII, Motu proprio
  << Rubricarum instructum >> diei 23 iulii anno i960 approbato posteroque die
  a Sacra Rituum Congregatione promulgato, vix fieri non potuit quin eadem
  Sacra Rituum Congregatio novam Missalis romani editionem, ad dictum
  rubricarum codicem plane accommodatam, pararet.

Operative clause: `hinc est quod praesens Vaticana Missalis romani editio uti
<< typica >> declaratur`. Dateline: `Romae, ex aedibus Sacrae Rituum
Congregationis, die 23 iunii 1962`, subscribed `A. M. Card. LARRAONA, S. R. C.
Praefectus` and `Henricus Dante, S. R. C. a secretis`.

So the incipit `Novo rubricarum corpore`, which this file expressly declined to
promote because it was known only from a report, is now read from the book.

WHY THE ERROR WAS MADE, because it is instructive and not careless. This
tracer's corpus is seven Internet Archive OCR text layers, and its 1962 witness
is the BENZIGER printing, which carries a New York imprimatur and not the
Vatican decree. The statement `only three occurrences of DECRETUM in 136,068
lines` was true of that scan. What was false was recording the result in a field
that reads as a claim about the repository -- because the repository held the
decree, in a passage record dated 2026-07-25, six days before this file was
written:
`passage.catholic-church.missale-romanum.vatican-typica-1962.decretum-sacrae-rituum-congregationis-1962`,
states `verified`, locus `front matter, artifact PDF p. 2`.

Two records of one fact, in one tree, never compared. guidance/the-shape.md
section 2. `act_citation` is `cited-externally` rather than `cited-in-corpus`
because the decree stands in the Vatican typical edition, which is not a witness
of this file's corpus; the corpus is unchanged and its own negative result
stands as reported.
source_record.amends:
`attested_in` NAMED ONLY A SUBSTITUTE. The base slice recorded this act as
attested in `benziger-iuxta-typicam-1962` -- a New York printing declared to
conform to the typical edition -- while the act's own `citation` field cited the
Vatican typical edition itself, by artifact id, at page 2 of the CMAA facsimile.
The corroborating witness was named and the controlling one was not, and the
reason it was not is that until this slice registered
`1962-missale-romanum-cmaa` above there was no row to name. That is the same
defect `5420ea2e7` found for the English on 2026-08-01 and `0032bd735` closed for
it on 2026-08-02; the Latin half of it stood until now.

THE BENZIGER IS KEPT AND IS NOT DEMOTED. It attests the same act at one remove,
through the conformity declaration its own row records, and it is the second scan
every corroboration in this repository runs against. What changes is that the
controlling witness now stands first and the record no longer names only the
substitute.

WHY THIS IS AN AMENDMENT HERE AND NOT AN EDIT THERE. The witness row belongs to
this slice: the base slice's `evidence` states in terms that nothing in it has
been read against a page image and that no row of it claims `page-image`, and
that is still true of it. An act in the base naming a witness only this file
carries would be a reference that resolves in the merged history and dangles in
the narrower one, so the reference is made where both ends stand.

NOTHING ELSE ABOUT THE ACT MOVES. `read_from` stays `ocr-only`, because the
decree at page 2 was read in the facsimile's OCR text layer and not off the page
-- the base slice quotes it with the recognition damage intact -- and the day,
the authority, the parentage, the reception basis and the effect are as the base
recorded them.

The merge is drawn because the reception is visible in the book itself, to the
letter, and not inferred from the fact that both acts precede it.

From the 1955 side: section 9 of Maxima redemptionis, fixing the Vigil at
midnight, is reproduced word for word in the witness. The Acta print it at
aas-47-1955 51915-51921 and the book prints it at benziger-iuxta-typicam-1962

From the 1960 side: the Code of Rubrics is printed entire in the same book's
front matter, from benziger-iuxta-typicam-1962 1276, with its promulgating decree
at 1235-1272 above it; and its renaming of the Introit is then carried through
into the Palm Sunday propers at 35155.

Where a reception cannot be shown like that, this file draws no merge, and
`act-history check` refuses any act with more than one parent that does not carry
this field.

S. Petrum, anno millesimo nongentesimo vicesimo quarto, sexto Idus Decembris, in
festo Immaculatae Conceptionis B. M. Virginis, praecipuae Lusitaniae Patronae,
Pontificatus Nostri anno tertio`, subscribed `A. Card. VICO, Ep. Portuen. et S.
Rufinae` and `Maurus Rigal, Canc. Ap. Tabularii Praefectus` [recorded: the
missal acquisition audit read the whole OCR text layer of the item on
2026-08-01; the item's byte sizes were re-verified here at the metadata API].

source_record.instrument: Bull Inter multiplices gravesque curas
source_record.root_basis:
The record of this line starts here. The Braga use is far older -- a 1558
printing is at the Bibliotheque nationale de France and a 1498 printing is
recorded with no digital facsimile located -- and neither is carried in this run,
so no edge is drawn into this station.

That makes this line unusual and worth noticing: it is the ONLY use line in this
file whose root is an act rather than a printing.

THE 1558 PRINTING WAS REACHED AND READ ON 2026-08-02, and this root is kept
anyway. It is BnF Réserve B-1478, 554 canvases, `Missale juxta usum & ordinem
Almae Bracarensis Ecclesiae Hispaniarum Primatis`, dated 1558 by Gallica's own
record, and its shelfmark is pencilled on the flyleaf at canvas f4 beside the
reference `Weale 198` [verified]. Two things in it are worth a later lane's
attention and NEITHER IS ASSERTED AS AN ACT HERE:

  1.  IT CARRIES WHAT LOOKS LIKE ITS OWN PROMULGATING INSTRUMENT. Canvas f5 is a
      letter headed `BALTHASAR LIMPVS ARCHIEPISCOPVS ET BRACARAE Dominus,
      Hispaniarum Primas: Decano & Capitulo sanctae Bracarensis Ecclesiae, ac
      totius eius prouinciae Clero sanctum exoptat spiritum & salutem in Domino
      sempiternam`, in which Archbishop Baltasar Limpo describes finding the old
      missal `corruptum illud certe vetustate` and having a corrected edition
      made [verified in the page image]. That is an archbishop of Braga ordering
      a Braga missal, four hundred years before the act this line is rooted on.
      IT IS NOT ADDED AS A STATION IN THIS RUN: the letter was read but not
      transcribed whole, it carries no date in the portion read, and adding a
      root below an existing root is a change to the line's shape rather than an
      evidence upgrade. It is the single most promising lead for extending this
      line backwards and it is written down so it is not re-found.

  2.  IT WAS PRINTED AT LYON, NOT AT BRAGA. Gallica's record gives the imprint
      as `Lugduni sumptibus Jo. à Burgundia, bibliopolae regis Lusitanorum,
      1558` [verified] -- at Lyon, at the charge of Jean de Bourgogne, bookseller
      to the King of Portugal. Worth recording because this file carries a
      Lyonnais line as well, and a reader meeting `Lugduni` on a Braga book
      should not take it for a use.

  3.  ONE CAUTION ON THE COPY. Its first printed leaf in the digitisation is the
      Limpo letter; no printed title page was found in the leaves examined, and
      the BnF describes the preliminaries as `[10]` leaves. Whether the title
      leaf is absent from this copy was NOT established, and it is flagged
      rather than resolved.

source_record.act_citation_note:
THE INSTRUMENT WAS NOT READ HERE AND IS BELIEVED TO EXIST. Its title and date
come from two documents that were read at the bytes: Summorum Pontificum names
it `Quattuor Abhinc Annos` beside Ecclesia Dei, and this repository's passage
record for Ecclesia Dei states that the motu proprio's footnote `identifies the
letter Quattuor abhinc annos of 3 October 1984` [recorded:
src/sources/works/john-paul-ii/ecclesia-dei/editions/english-vatican-web-2026-07-25/passages/complete-text.toml].

So the act is named, dated and twice attested by later instruments, and its own
text has not been read. `not-found` is exactly that state, and it is not
`none-claimed`: an instrument is claimed here and is missing, which is a
different thing from a printing for which no instrument is claimed at all.
source_record.act_citation_scope:
ADDED 2026-08-01, and THE SEARCH IT RECORDS FOUND SOMETHING. This is section
7.2's correction happening a second time, caught this time by the rule that
correction produced.

Searched: THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN SOURCE LIBRARY, for `quattuor abhinc annos`,
case-insensitively. Four files answer. Two are inventories, one is the Ecclesia
Dei passage record this note already cites -- and the fourth is
src/sources/works/holy-see/acta-apostolicae-sedis/editions/volume-76-1984/edition.toml,
whose own notes read that the complete 1984 volume `carries the Congregation for
Divine Worship's letter of 3 October 1984 on the use of the Roman Missal of 1962
(Quattuor abhinc annos) at pp. 1088-1089`. That edition has a registered OCR PDF
artifact beneath it.

SO THE INSTRUMENT IS AT NAMED PAGES OF A VOLUME THIS REPOSITORY ALREADY HOLDS,
and `not-found` here means not in the missal corpus this slice reads. The value
is left as it stands because promoting it is a claim that somebody READ the
letter, and nobody has; naming a document and reading it are different acts. The
next lane to touch this station should open pages 1088-1089 of that artifact,
and the station should then become `cited-in-corpus`.
source_record.authority: Sacred Congregation for Divine Worship, by mandate of John Paul II
source_record.citation: Sacred Congregation for Divine Worship, Quattuor abhinc annos, 3 October 1984, as named in Summorum Pontificum and in the footnotes of Ecclesia Dei.
source_record.effect: No departure. It governs use, not text.

source_record.parent_basis:
A FORK, not a merge: one parent, on another line, which is how a line is born.
The edge is drawn because Summorum Pontificum, read here at the bytes, names
this letter and Ecclesia Dei as `the previous documents` laying down `the
conditions for the use of THIS MISSAL` -- the Missal `promulgated by Blessed
John XXIII in 1962`. The act's subject is the 1962 typical edition, so the edge
runs from that station.

source_record.amends:
QUO PRIMUM IS NO LONGER A ROOT. The base slice drew it as one and said in terms
that it took no position on what preceded it. This slice goes earlier, and the
edge it draws is not a guess: the bull's own opening recites the Tridentine
decree that committed the missal to the Pope. An act that says what it is
executing has drawn its own edge.

The base slice's root basis is kept, not deleted, and is printed as superseded.
It was correct about its own corpus, and a record that quietly stops saying
something it once said is a record a reader cannot check.

source_record.citation: Pius V, Quo primum tempore, 14 July 1570, printed in the front matter of the witnesses below.

source_record.instrument: Apostolic constitution Quo primum tempore
source_record.parent_basis:
The bull recites the decree it is executing: among the other decrees of the
Sacred Tridentine Council it fell to us to determine concerning the sacred
books, the Catechism, the Missal and the Breviary, to be issued and emended.
Read here in the base slice's own 1862 witness [corpus].

(..umque
inter  alia  Sacri  Tridentini  Concilii  decreta,  nobis  statuendum  esset  de
sacris  libris,  Catechismo,  Missali,  et  Breviario  edendis,  atque  emendan-
dis:  edito  jam,  Deo  ipso  annuente,  ad  populi  eruditionem  Catecbismo,
et  ad  debitas  Deo  persolvendas  laudes  Breviario  castigato
source_record.promulgation_note: Posted at the doors of St Peter's and of the Apostolic Chancery on 29 July 1570, per the subscription printed after the bull in pustet-1862 (OCR lines 276-282).
source_record.root_basis_superseded:
Superseded on 2026-08-01 by the edge above. What it said:

  The earliest act this tracer represents. It is not the beginning of the Roman
  Mass and is not offered as one: what stands before it -- the pre-Tridentine
  curial missal, the 1474 Milan printing, the diocesan uses out of which the
  Tridentine commission worked -- is a live question this tracer takes no
  position on and draws no edge into. A root here means "this record starts
  here", not "nothing preceded it".

Its parenthetical list is still right about the 1474 printing and the diocesan
uses: this slice draws NO edge from any of them into Quo primum either, and the
pre-Tridentine Roman printings it does carry stand on their own line and stop
before 1570. What changed is only that the Tridentine mandate, which the bull
itself cites, is now carried. The quotation supporting the new edge stands at
pustet-1862 OCR lines 158-164, with OCR damage reproduced, including `(..umque`
for `Cumque` and `Catecbismo` for `Catechismo`.

source_record.act_citation_note:
NO INSTRUMENT WAS LOCATED, AND ONE IS BELIEVED TO EXIST. A reprint described as
EMENDED was emended by someone; the 2002 book records the state and not the act.

This station is drawn because omitting it would make a postconciliar recension
silently wrong about 1971 to 1975, and the omission would be invisible: the
missal acquisition audit found this reprint by READING a leaf rather than by
searching, and recorded that a record omitting it `will be silently wrong`.

The value is `not-found` and NOT `none-claimed`, and the difference is the whole
point of having both. A `printed` station claims no act at all; this one says an
act is missing.

The date is `1971` with `date_precision = "year"`, which is what the leaf gives.
No day is invented to make it sort.
source_record.act_citation_scope:
ADDED 2026-08-01, when `check` began requiring a not-found to name what was
searched (guidance/act-histories.md section 10, item 2). The bound is stated
from what this record can support and no more.

Searched: THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN SOURCE LIBRARY, for `reimpressio`, which returns
fifteen files. They are this slice, four other inventories, one calendar, the
2008 Variationes work and its Notitiae edition, a segment record of the 2002
typical edition, and a work record for the 2008 NOTICE of the emended reprint --
that is, records ABOUT the reprint and none of the reprint's own instrument.

NOT searched: the Acta Apostolicae Sedis for 1971, Notitiae for 1971, and the
front matter of any 1971 printing. Not found here means not in the tree and not
in the witnesses this slice declares. It is not a statement about any archive.

source_record.authority: John XXIII
source_record.citation: John XXIII, Rubricarum instructum, 25 July 1960, printed in the front matter of the 1962 witness.
source_record.dateline: Datum Romae, apud S. Petrum, die 25 mensis Iulii, anno 1960, Pontificatus Nostri secundo.
source_record.effect: No departure in this slice; it approves the code, which the next act promulgates.
source_record.effect_note:
This act and the one after it are two halves of one thing and are kept apart
because they are two instruments with two dates and two authorities. The motu
proprio approves the code and orders the Congregation to promulgate it; the
Congregation's decree of the following day promulgates it. Collapsing them would
lose a day, an authority and a document.
source_record.instrument: Apostolic letter motu proprio Rubricarum instructum
source_record.parent_basis:
The motu proprio names its predecessor and disposes of it: it declares that the
general Decree of the Sacred Congregation of Rites of 23 March 1955 De rubricis
ad simpliciorem formam redigendis ceases to be in force, having been taken up
into this new redaction of the rubrics. An act that says what it supersedes has
drawn its own edge.
source_record.parent_quotation:

generale S. R. C. diei 23 Martii anni 1955 l)e rubricU atl $impliciorem formam re-
difxeutlis, in hac nova rubricarum redactione assumptum.

source_record.effect: No departure in this slice.
source_record.effect_note:
A station that writes no row on purpose, and the third such in this history. The
constitution orders the rite of the Mass to be revised; it revises nothing
itself, and every unit that moved moved at the books the later acts promulgated.
It is carried because the constitution of 1969 states in its own title that the
Missal was restored BY DECREE OF THIS COUNCIL, so leaving it out would make the
act of 1969 look like a papal initiative standing on nothing.
source_record.instrument: Constitution on the Sacred Liturgy Sacrosanctum Concilium
source_record.parent_basis:
The state the constitution legislated for is the one the 1962 typical edition
carried: that was the missal in use when it was promulgated, eighteen months
after the edition was declared typical. Nothing in Sacrosanctum Concilium names
the 1962 edition, so the edge says where the station sits and not what it
inherited.

source_record.authority: Francis
source_record.citation: Francis, Traditionis custodes, 16 July 2021, English text on vatican.va.
source_record.dateline: Given at Rome, at Saint John Lateran, on 16 July 2021, the liturgical Memorial of Our Lady of Mount Carmel, in the ninth year of Our Pontificate. FRANCIS
source_record.effect: No departure in this file, and this station is where the line's whole point becomes visible.
source_record.effect_note:
NOTHING ON THIS LINE MOVES A TEXT, and that is why the line exists separately.
Article 1 declares the postconciliar books the unique expression of the lex
orandi of the Roman Rite; Summorum Pontificum article 1 had called the 1962
edition an extraordinary form of the same rite and said it was never abrogated.
The two are in the record, dated, quoted and NOT reconciled. No merge is drawn
between this line and the Roman one, because a merge asserts a reception and
what these documents show is the opposite.
source_record.in_force: immediately on publication in L'Osservatore Romano, by the letter's own order

source_record.parent_basis:
Article 8 abrogates what stands before it: previous norms, instructions,
permissions, and customs that do not conform to the provisions of the present
Motu Proprio are abrogated. An act that disposes of its predecessors has drawn
its own edge, and the nearest of those predecessors on this line is the
instruction of 2011.
source_record.parent_quotation:
Art. 1. The liturgical books promulgated by Saint Paul VI and Saint John Paul
II, in conformity with the decrees of Vatican Council II, are the unique
expression of the lex orandi of the Roman Rite.
[...]
Art. 8. Previous norms, instructions, permissions, and customs that do not
conform to the provisions of the present Motu Proprio are abrogated.
source_record.read_from_note: As for Summorum Pontificum: a born-digital delivery, read at the bytes, for which the three-value reading vocabulary has no exact term.

source_record.authority: The Council of Trent, under Pius IV
source_record.citation: Council of Trent, Session XXII, 17 September 1562, Decretum de observandis et evitandis in celebratione missae, in Canones et decreta sacrosancti oecumenici Concilii Tridentini, Leipzig: Tauchnitz, 1887, printed p. 121.
source_record.dateline: SESSIO XXII. QUAE EST SEXTA SUB PIO IV. PONT. MAX., CELEBRATA DIE XVII. SEPTEMBR^S MDLXII
source_record.effect: No departure in this slice. It is the act that makes the Tridentine reform of the missal an answer to something.
source_record.effect_note:
Not a claim that it changed nothing. The decree legislates against abuses --
avarice, irreverence, superstition -- and commits their suppression to the local
ordinaries; it does not itself revise a formulary, and no unit of this slice was
read against it.
source_record.instrument: Decretum de observandis et evitandis in celebratione missae, Session XXII
source_record.locus: 1887-canones-et-decreta-tridentini OCR lines 6287-6355; the session's own heading at 6024-6032
source_record.quotation:
DECRETUM  DE  OBSERVANDIS  ET  EVITANDIS  IN  CE-
LEBR ATIONE  MISSAE.
Quanta  cura  adhibenda  sit,  ut  sacrosanctum  missae  sa-
crificium  omui  religionis  cultu  ac  veneratione  celebretur
[...]
decernit  sancta  synodus,  ut  ordinarii
Iocorum  episcopi  ea  omnia  prohibere  atque  e  medio  tollere
sedulo  curent  ac  teneantur,  quae  vel  avaritia,  idolorum  ser-
vitus,  vel  irreverentia,  quae  ab  impietate  vix  seiuncta  esse
potest,  vel  superstitio,  verae  pietatis  falsa  imitatrix,  induxit.
source_record.quotation_note:
Reproduced with its OCR damage (`omui` for `omni`, `Iocorum` for `locorum`,
`LEBR ATIONE` broken by the scan). The elision spans the decree's opening
argument and a running header.
source_record.root_basis:
The earliest act this file carries, and it is not offered as the beginning of
anything. What stands before it -- the mediaeval Roman curial missal, the
sacramentaries behind that, the uses out of which all of them grew -- is not
represented here and no edge is drawn into this station. A root means the record
starts here.

It is the earliest act rather than the Session XXV decree because it is the
Council's own act about the CELEBRATION OF MASS, and because the reform Quo
primum executed answers the abuses this decree names.
source_record.title: Trent orders the abuses in the celebration of Mass put down

entries.title: Trent orders the abuses in the celebration of Mass put down

source_record.authority: The Council of Trent, under Pius IV
source_record.citation: Council of Trent, Session XXV, concluded 4 December 1563, De indice librorum et catechismo, breviario et missali, in the Tauchnitz edition of 1887.
source_record.dateline: SESSIO XXV. QUAE EST NONA ET ULTIMA SUB PIO IV. PONT. MAX., COEPTA DIE III., ABSOLUTA DIE IV. DECEMBRIS MDLXIIl.
source_record.effect: Refers the missal to the Roman Pontiff. This is the act Quo primum executes, and Quo primum says so.
source_record.instrument: Decretum de indice librorum et catechismo, breviario et missali, Session XXV
source_record.locus: 1887-canones-et-decreta-tridentini OCR lines 10736-10762; the session's heading at 9021-9028
source_record.parent_basis:
Two acts of one council, in the order the council took them, and nothing in
either names the other: the Session XXV decree recites Session II, not Session
XXII. The edge says where this station sits, not what it inherited, which is
what `line-order` means and why it is the weakest kind.
source_record.quotation:
De  indice  librnrum  et  catechismo ,  breviario  et  missafi.
[...]
praecipit,  ut  quicquid  ab  illis  prae-
stitum  est  sanctissimo  Romano  Pontifici  exhibeatur,  ut  eius
iudicio  atque  auctoritate  terminetur  et  evulgetur.  Idemque
de  catechismo  a  Patribus,  quibus  illud  uiaudatuni  fuerat,
et  de  missali  et  breviario  fieri  mandat.
source_record.quotation_note:
OCR damage reproduced: `librnrum` and `missafi` in the heading, `uiaudatuni` for
`mandatum`. The operative sentence is the last: the same is ordered to be done
concerning the missal and the breviary -- that is, referred to the Roman Pontiff
for his judgement and authority, which is what Quo primum then says it is doing.
source_record.title: Trent commits the missal to the Roman Pontiff

stages.label: Demetrius adds diptych material
stages.limitations: Proposed motive for the addition is the scholar’s inference. This is not a new whole-book edition.
stages.reception: Same composite Sinai witness; subsequent use and descent unestablished.

evidence.claim: Explicitly identifies the 1692 Vilnius codification.

evidence.claim: Names first insertion at Univ in 1733 and subsequent eighteenth-century reprinting.

stages.label: Expanded order for the read Liturgy
stages.limitations: Individual source-book rubrics not collated; cannot assign every later practice to 1733.

evidence.claim: Identifies full Lviv 1905 Sluzhebnik and its eight provisions.
Identifies the 1905 book as widely used before Roman revision.

stages.label: Lviv’s eight provisions for private celebration
stages.limitations: Book’s own pages not acquired; no direct descent from Univ 1733 established.
stages.reception: Institution reports use in Europe and America; extent and uniformity not quantified.
stages.scope: Private/read-Liturgy provisions only
stages.summary: Eight provisions are the explicit object of the later circular’s corrections.
stages.witness_label: Full Lviv Sluzhebnik, 1905

stages.date_label: Attested by 10 September 1941 circulars; underlying Chrysostom book published 1940

evidence.claim: Records omission and other qualified rubrics.
Explains changes from Lviv 1905.

stages.label: Revised Ruthenian Chrysostom book and implementation rules
stages.limitations: 1941 clarifications are not a separately asserted new printing. Whole book uncollated. The positioned date is the attestation of implementing rules, not a new 1941 printing or the start of universal use.
stages.reception: Circular I preserves territorial rules and older clergy’s private customary use; formation houses directed to new books.
stages.scope: Chrysostom text/rubrics, with separate implementing circulars
stages.summary: Pre-epiclesis troparia omitted; private celebration follows common ceremonies with specified accommodations.
stages.witness_label: Sancta et divina Liturgia S. Joannis Chrysostomi, Rome, 1940; circulars I–II, 1941

evidence.claim: Names the full volume and distinguishes Ruthenian feasts from Russian material.

stages.label: Full Ruthenian Liturgikon assembled
stages.limitations: Assembly is not proof of changed Chrysostom wording; no 1940→1942 textual revision asserted.
stages.reception: Ruthenian recension; particular Churches’ actual adoption remains separately evidenced.
stages.scope: Complementary liturgies, daily offices and calendar material
stages.summary: Full volume gathers the previously issued components and supplementary/calendar material.

evidence.claim: Explicitly contrasts Russian-use policy with Ruthenian § 2.

stages.label: Russian-use Chrysostom book
stages.limitations: Russian precursor printing unidentified; do not manufacture a Russian-Synodal predecessor node.
stages.reception: Prepared for Catholic clergy following Russian usage; not a Ruthenian successor.
stages.scope: Commemorations and pre-epiclesis rubric policy
stages.summary: Papal commemoration replaces the Synod reference; pre-epiclesis troparia retained with optional omission.
stages.witness_label: Divina Liturgia S. Joannis Chrysostomi, Rome 1940, 112 pages (Raes)

evidence.claim: Identifies complete book and Russian commemorations.
Distinguishes the later addition from this calendar state.

stages.label: Full Russian-use Sluzhebnik assembled
stages.limitations: Assembly does not establish another revision of 1940 prayers.
stages.reception: Russian-use Catholic recension; Bulgarian/Serbian local receipt not shown here.

stages.witness_label: Služebnik, Rome 1942, 691+49 pages (Raes)

evidence.claim: Identifies addition and source-book locator.

stages.label: All Saints of Rus added to calendar supplement
stages.limitations: Exact 1953 pages not inspected; no claim of a complete edition diff.
stages.reception: Addition within the Catholic Vulgata publication; use frequency not established.
stages.scope: Named movable commemoration and its liturgical propers
stages.summary: Adds All Saints of Rus on the second Sunday after Pentecost with specified proper chants.

evidence.claim: Paleographic date, arrangement and edited Syriac anaphora distinguish the original portion from thirteenth-century additions.

stages.label: Mar Eshaya: anaphora without written private prayers
stages.limitations: The date is approximate; later additions cannot be backdated. Absence from a Hudra does not alone prove a prayer was never said. No second/third-century composition date inferred.
stages.reception: Church of the East manuscript heritage; no claim of medieval Chaldean Catholic reception.
stages.scope: Original anaphoral portion of a Hudra that also preserves Theodore and Nestorius; not a reconstructed complete missal.
stages.summary: Addai and Mari is written without the kushshaphe and without an institution narrative. The Hudra places Theodore at Christmas, Nestorius at Epiphany, and the Apostles after Easter baptism.
stages.witness_label: Mosul, Mar Eshaya Hudra, Apostles anaphora manuscript pp. 463–466

evidence.claim: Identifies and dates the witness and explicitly reports its kushshaphe.

stages.label: Diarbekir: private prayers written with the anaphora
stages.limitations: The surviving volume covers entry into Lent to the end of Easter week. Missing Christmas/Epiphany sections are a volume-survival issue, not suppression of their anaphoras. No universal introduction date established.
stages.reception: Historical Church of the East witness; modern Catholic ownership/location would not establish original Catholic use.
stages.scope: Apostles anaphora in one volume of a formerly three-volume Hudra.
stages.summary: This witness includes the private celebrant prayers normally preceding the ghanta, unlike the Mar Eshaya text.
stages.witness_label: Diarbekir Hudra, surviving second volume, Macomber siglum B

evidence.claim: Date 1287 and omission; possible older exemplar or local nonrecognition discussed.

stages.label: Mardin 22: older form still written without private prayers
stages.limitations: Macomber treats abbreviated Hudra copying and local nonrecognition as alternatives requiring care. This does not establish a 1287 reform removing prayers.
stages.reception: Church of the East heritage, not evidence that the Catholic recension existed in 1287.
stages.scope: Anaphoral text within a surviving second Hudra volume.
stages.summary: The kushshaphe are absent in this dated later witness, showing that manuscript forms cannot be arranged as a simple universal progression.
stages.witness_label: Mardin 22, Hudra, Macomber siglum C

evidence.claim: Identifies the complete 1767 Catholic Propaganda edition.
Identifies Cr as 1767 pp. 280–286 and distinguishes the older printed omission from the later Mosul reading.
evidence.locus: p. 357 siglum Cr; p. 366 line 53 apparatus; p. 345 note 2

stages.label: Rome: Catholic Propaganda missal recension
stages.limitations: The full 1767 book is not page-collated. No claim of first Catholic printing or a complete list of Latin/Maronite additions. Institution placement at the fraction remains an acquisition gap.
stages.reception: Publication by the Roman Propaganda Congregation identifies a Catholic book; breadth and continuity of local adoption not independently established.
stages.scope: Catholic printed witness; bounded Addai and Mari readings established through the critical apparatus, full ordinary not yet inspected.
stages.summary: Macomber’s Cr witness supplies an identifiable Catholic printed state. Its intercession omits the phrase about the life-giving Gospel that is present in the ancient witness and modern Mosul editions.
stages.witness_label: Missale Chaldaicum ex decreto Sacrae Congregationis de Propaganda Fide editum (Rome, 1767)

evidence.claim: Native beginning and 1901 imprimatur inspected.
Complementary proper volume shares the 1901 Mosul Dominican imprint.
Specifies 1901 pp. 24–36 as Cm 01 and records the relevant anaphoral readings.
evidence.locus: p. 357 Cm 01; p. 363 note 10; p. 366 line 53 apparatus

stages.label: Mosul: ordinary and complementary propers
stages.limitations: The companion volume is not a second stage. 1901 attests these readings; it does not date their introduction. Macomber also finds the post-Sanctus insertion in a late nineteenth-century Mar Ya‘qob ritual.
stages.reception: Catholic imprimatur from Henricus Altmayer, Apostolic Delegate, 22 October 1901. It authorizes printing; it does not establish universal use or an independent complete reform.
stages.scope: One publication state represented by complementary ordinary/anaphoral and temporal-sanctoral proper volumes.
stages.summary: The ordinary prints the expanded Lord’s Prayer near the beginning. In Addai and Mari, Macomber locates the institution narrative at the opening of the post-Sanctus prayer and records the life-giving Gospel phrase in the intercession.
stages.witness_label: Missale juxta ritum Ecclesiae Syrorum Orientalium, id est Chaldaeorum; companion Proprium missarum de tempore et de sanctis (Mosul, Dominican press, 1901)

evidence.claim: Reports 2005 synod, 18 February 2006 recognitio, and 6 January 2007 implementation date.
Describes rearrangement, litanies and audible recitation.
Sako disputes broad reception of the printed reform and whether it incorporated the synod’s corrections.

stages.label: Reformed Taksa associated with Jammo
stages.limitations: No original Syriac 2007 edition acquired. Two Internet Archive English aids were found; neither is silently substituted for a native text. The effective date is the reported synodal decision, not proof of universal implementation.
stages.reception: Jammo states St Peter’s diocese would implement. Sako later disputes wider acceptance and whether the printed text included synodal corrections; these accounts are not collapsed into universal reception.
stages.scope: Identifiable reform described by its compiler and scholarly observer; text identity and reception distinguished.
stages.summary: The reform places the institution narrative after the intercessions, before the epiclesis/anamnesis sequence, and directs audible anaphoral recitation. Royel also describes removal of diaconal exhortations around the Pax.
stages.witness_label: Reformed Takhsa d-Raze, approved 2005/recognized 2006 according to Jammo; original Syriac edition still to acquire

evidence.claim: Title, opening and rubrics image checked.
The Congregation exceptionally grants the proposed modifications recognitio ad quinquennium on 20 October 2014.

stages.label: Baghdad: five-year trial order of the Apostles
stages.limitations: The 35-page institutional PDF is not a full annual missal set. No complete transcription. Its 2015 PDF metadata does not replace the 2014 book date.
stages.reception: Patriarchal preface 27 October 2014 presents the trial order for the Chaldean Church. Authoritative direction and actual parish compliance remain distinct.
stages.scope: Printed Addai and Mari order with official letter, patriarchal introduction and new practical rubrics.
stages.summary: The native opening omits the expanded Lord’s Prayer; its Gloria and conditional psalmody lead to the opening prayer. Rubrics require audible prayer and distinguish the priest’s initial orientation from the offertory facing the people.
stages.witness_label: رتبة القداس بحسب الطقس الكلداني / The Order of the Mass: The Liturgy of the Blessed Apostles (Baghdad, 2014), Syriac/Arabic

evidence.claim: Reports revision of Theodore, new Thomas order reviewed in 2019, confirmation 20 November 2019 and 2020 publication.
evidence.locus: تجديد2014–2020, paragraphs on the second anaphora and Thomas

evidence.claim: Confirms contents and native Syriac/Arabic presentation of the later reprint.
evidence.locus: Contents PDF 173; Thomas printed p. 81/PDF 87; preface iii–iv

evidence.claim: Identifies 2025 as reprint of the exhausted 2020 collection.

stages.label: Baghdad: revised collection with new Thomas order
stages.limitations: Original 2020 impression and approval act not acquired. November 2025 notice loosely calls confirmation 2020; keep exact 2019 date attributed to Sako pending act inspection. 2025 typographic/linguistic corrections are not a separately proved reform.
stages.reception: Official patriarchal collection; publisher prescribes common use. Actual use in every eparchy is not established by publication. Arabic/Sureth/English translation histories remain separate.
stages.scope: Collection of Sunday/feast and weekday Apostles orders, Thomas order, and second anaphora; 2025 reprint used only as a later witness.
stages.summary: The collection incorporates a newly composed order named for Thomas alongside revised existing orders. The 2025 contents visibly separates Sunday/feast, weekday, Thomas, and second anaphora sections.
stages.witness_label: رُتب القداس بحسب الطقس الكلداني (Baghdad, 2020), witnessed by the official 2025 reprint Chaldean Catholic Missal

evidence.claim: Explicit reforms of the 1601 and 1605 chapters; full conformity in the Canon, limited conformity elsewhere.
Three bounded prayer units directly transcribed from page images.

stages.label: 1606 Romanizing Cistercian missal
stages.limitations: This is already a revised state, not a proxy for all medieval Cistercian practice. The exact 1606 witness has now been split from the earlier broad printed-witness cluster. No claim that every decree of 1601 or 1605 was fully received locally.
stages.reception: The book identifies itself as for the Cistercian Order and invokes chapter authority; no monastery-by-monastery reception census has been made.
stages.scope: Printed order missal implementing Roman conformity in the Canon while retaining Cistercian usages elsewhere.
stages.summary: The 1606 Annotanda attributes full Roman conformity in the Canon to the 1601 and 1605 general chapters, and conformity elsewhere only as proper Cistercian use allows. The printed Ordinary still has a short Confiteor, a combined Suscipe Trinitas offering, and Orate/Dominus sit response.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum Sacri Ordinis Cisterciensis, Paris, Dionysia Cavellat, 1606; BSB 2 Liturg. 205 a

evidence.claim: The general chapter held in May 1651 authorized three learned men to correct the books; the 1655 mandate extends the printing privilege.
Primary description of the new revision; retained graduals prevent complete Roman imitation.
Three complete paired prayers and their position in the offertory read from images.

stages.label: 1657 further Roman correction
stages.limitations: The 1651 commission, 1655 mandate, and 1657 publication are distinct dates. The inspected 1655 instrument is not a universal effective-date decree. The Monitum historical catalogue of earlier defects must not all be assigned specifically to 1606.
stages.reception: The Cistercian superior authorizes the edition and printing monopoly; this is evidence of intended order use, not uniform local implementation.
stages.scope: Printed Cistercian missal following the 1651 commission; a substantially Romanized Ordinary while retaining order-specific material.
stages.summary: The Ordinary enlarges the Confiteor with named saints including Bernard and triple culpa; replaces the old Orate and response; prints separate host and chalice offerings and a revised Suscipe Trinitas after Lavabo. The Monitum reports reordered Pentecost-to-Advent Sunday Masses and Roman rubrics, but expressly retains differences in the graduals.
stages.witness_label: Missale Cisterciense iuxta Romani recogniti correctionem, Paris, Sebastianus and Gabriel Cramoisy, 1657; Krzeszów copy, FIDES 3755

evidence.claim: Venice 1550 is printed on the title.
The named formulary and texts are visible on the identified folios.

stages.label: Venice witness before the Xavierre revision
stages.limitations: This does not reconstruct the full 1550 missal, identify its immediate exemplar, or establish how long each house used it.
stages.reception: The title identifies the Dominican use. A printed intended-use statement does not prove reception in every province.
stages.scope: Suscepimus Deus formulary within the temporale.
stages.summary: Suscepimus Deus appears under Dominica octava, with Deus cuius providentia as collect and Attendite a falsis prophetis as Gospel.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum fratrum Praedicatorum Sancti Dominici, Venice, 1550

evidence.claim: Printing dated 1604, under Hieronymus Xavierre.
The editor explicitly describes conformity of Epistles and Gospels to Roman use.
The revised combination is directly visible.

stages.label: Xavierre revision witnessed in the Rome printing
stages.limitations: The original intervention predates this printing; 1604 is not assigned as the first promulgation or first revised edition. Only the selected formulary is text-collated.
stages.reception: Clement VIII’s brief dated 2 April 1602 preserves the Order’s rite while authorizing conformity in specified matters. Its adoption windows depend on place and availability of copies; actual local uptake is not established.
stages.scope: A revised temporale formulary and the revision’s reprinted authorizing documents.
stages.summary: Suscepimus Deus now has Largire nobis as collect and the unjust-steward Gospel, with its heading moved to Dominica sexta after the octave of Trinity.
stages.witness_label: Missale juxta ritum sacri ordinis Praedicatorum S. P. N. Dominici, Rome, ex typographia Alfonsi Ciacconi, apud Carolum Vulliettum, 1604

evidence.claim: Imprint is Venice, Giunta, 1574; the book identifies the Carmelite observance and custom of Jerusalem.
These printed entries are directly visible.

stages.label: Carmelite October calendar before the later additions
stages.limitations: Calendar absence on one date is not proof that a saint or devotion is absent from every section of the volume.
stages.reception: This is the Carmelite Latin book identified by its own title. The title’s Jerusalem claim is recorded without constructing a genealogy from it.
stages.scope: Printed October calendar.
stages.summary: October 5 has no printed feast. October 6 includes Abraham, Isaac and Jacob with three lessons and the octave of Michael; October 8 includes Simeon the prophet.
stages.witness_label: Missale antique professionis Regularium beatissime Dei genitricis semperque virginis Marie de Monte Carmelo, Venice: Giunta, 1574

evidence.claim: The 1621 printing is described as printed again, with chapter and Prior General authority.
Teresa’s feast and common-Mass reference are printed, distinct from marginal handwriting.
The instrument is dated 26 September 1584, not 1621.

stages.label: Carmelite calendar with Teresa of Jesus
stages.limitations: Neither the exact introduction date of Teresa’s feast nor the date of the chapter decree is established. Manuscript corrections in this copy are excluded.
stages.reception: The printed book belongs to the Carmelite ancient-observance sequence. A handwritten direction to a Discalced missal on p. 409 is not treated as the printed rite’s prescription.
stages.scope: Printed October calendar and Teresa’s printed common-Mass reference.
stages.summary: October 5 prints Teresa as duplex minus with a commemoration of Placidus and companions. Teresa’s sanctoral entry directs the reader to the common Dilexisti iustitiam Mass.
stages.witness_label: Missale fratrum Carmelitarum Ordinis Beatae Dei Genitricis Mariae de monte Carmelo, Venice: Giunta, 1621

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1538 witness.
Colophon and comparison identify this state.

stages.scope: Identified edition, represented through critical discussion of its Ordo and Palm Sunday.

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1558 witness.

stages.reception: Revision for Braga. Limpo’s Carmelite membership does not establish derivation from a Carmelite missal; Carvalho rejects direct dependence on the Carmelite 1551 and Lyon 1556 books he compared.
stages.scope: Reported changes to the Ordo and Palm Sunday blessing.
stages.summary: Limpo’s revision changes the Ordo and Palm Sunday blessing.
stages.witness_label: Missale juxta usum et ordinem Almae Bracarensis Ecclesiae, Lyon: Petrus Fradin, 1558; BnF B-1478

evidence.claim: Identifies the revised 1924 Vatican printing.
The dateline is 8 December 1924; it directs the archdiocese’s priests to this missal.
The decree dated 9 December 1924 declares the edition typical and sets the future conformity and feast-insertion rules.

stages.label: Braga typical edition approved in December 1924
stages.limitations: These rules describe the 1924 state; their absence from 1558 has not been established. Later inserted feasts in this copy must not be assigned to 1924.
stages.reception: The bull requires this missal for priests of the Archdiocese of Braga. This establishes the contemporary prescription, not universal subsequent observance or present law.
stages.scope: The title edition and its binding approval/conformity rules; no complete body reconstruction.
stages.summary: Approved 8 December and declared typical 9 December 1924. Future Holy See changes to Masses already contained in it must be applied; newly imposed universal feasts must enter the Braga calendar.
stages.witness_label: Missale Bracarense, Rome: Typis Polyglottis Vaticanis, 1924; title edition distinct from the digitized copy’s later supplements

evidence.claim: Lists separate 1774 ordinary, 1775 sacramental ritual and 1775 rites-and-lections titles.
Describes prayer, ritual and calendar additions associated with the first printed Taksa.

stages.label: First Roman printed ordinary and lection collection
stages.limitations: No original 1774/1775 page comparison. The two Eucharistic books are not two successive revisions. The retrospective does not securely assign every item to an individual volume.
stages.reception: Prepared for Malabar Catholic worship; no claim that every reported addition originated in 1774.
stages.scope: Complementary Eucharistic volumes; the sacramental ritual is excluded.

evidence.claim: Explicitly names Propaganda printings of 1775 and 1845 and describes the earlier arrangement.

Do not equate it with the separately reported 1844 lection book or 1845 sacramental ritual.
stages.reception: An authorized editorial exemplar for the 1906 Malabar book; its actual historical use is not reconstructed.
stages.scope: Bounded earlier arrangement and absence of the later-approved appended Masses, as described in the 1904/1905 permissions.
stages.summary: The permission describes an exemplar with dispersed ordinary material and Rogation readings in a supplement.

evidence.claim: Directs collection of the ordinary and relocation of Rogation readings.

evidence.locus: Physical PDF 6, 15 October 1905 approval and 1906 imprint

stages.label: Reorganized travel missal with appended Masses
stages.limitations: The censor’s report is primary evidence of additions, not our collation. Names and precise Syriac loci of the appended Masses remain unverified.
stages.reception: Printing authorized by Aloysius Pareparambil for Malabar Catholic use; no wider normative replacement is inferred.
stages.scope: Andreas Kalapura edition: arrangement and additions explicitly described in its permissions.

evidence.claim: Describes the edition against which Vadakel’s changes are stated.

stages.label: Roman exemplar described by the 1946 editor
stages.limitations: No date or exact Roman printing is named. This contextual state cannot be merged with the 1845 exemplar without further evidence.
stages.reception: Malabar liturgical exemplar, not the Latin Roman Missal; the phrase Roman Edition indicates printing context here.
stages.scope: Only features explicitly contrasted by the 1946 foreword.
stages.summary: Prayers/rubrics were dispersed; some feasts appeared only in the calendar; server prayers were merely indicated; Marian Huthama was absent.
stages.witness_label: Unidentified Roman edition named in Augustine Kandathil’s foreword to Vadakel 1946

evidence.claim: Dates the printing and explicitly describes the changed content and arrangement.

evidence.claim: Names Holy See letter Prot. 2521/28 of 3 September 1930 for double-asterisk feasts and the Immaculate Conception Gospel.

stages.summary: Regroups and brackets transferred material, supplies proper and server texts, and preserves a Nineveh appendix with Marian Huthama.

evidence.claim: Identifies the Latin consultative text and its component page ranges.

stages.limitations: Book not acquired. Publication in 1955 is distinct from approval on 26 June 1957 and reception in 1962.

evidence.claim: Separates 20 January promulgation from 3 July introduction and identifies omitted components.

stages.label: Partial restoration introduced in worship
stages.limitations: A reception stage, not a new original-language revision inferred from translation. Original instruction and complete book not inspected.
stages.reception: Syro-Malabar episcopal introduction; not proof of uniform practice in every parish.
stages.scope: Community reception of a restricted restored order; independent Malayalam translation history deferred.
stages.summary: The bishops introduced the bilingual order on 3 July; several approved restored components remained unimplemented.

evidence.claim: Confirms year, typical-edition designation and native Syriac content.
evidence.locus: Physical PDF 3–5, English/Syriac title leaves and first rubric leaf

stages.label: 2003 Syriac typical-edition witness
stages.limitations: Do not count as an established substantive new stage solely from the title. No full book, approval decree or changed-text statement obtained.
stages.reception: Title says use of the Church of the East Syrians of Malabar; Catholic bibliographic context corroborated by commission-hosted source list.

stages.summary: James is revised against older manuscripts and Greek; John Evangelist is followed by Twelve Apostles, Basil of Caesarea, Mark, Eustathius and Cyril of Jerusalem. The editor suppresses Peter/Xystus and rejects three 1843 attributions. He removes conclusions after individual James diptychs; replaces the fraction/consignation formula with “Panem coelestem frangimus”; restores entrance prayers and changes Holy Thursday/Holy Saturday and dismissal prayers. The Presanctified rite is replaced, and solemn-celebration rubrics and preparatory/concluding prayers are added. Arabic is printed beside appropriate Syriac public prayers.
